name: Anavar / oxandrolone voice risk
lead: Oxandrolone, sold as Oxandrin and colloquially known as Anavar, is an oral synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid. Its article lists voice deepening among the virilizing effects in women, and states that such masculinizing changes can be irreversible.[1]

Women using it for physique purposes have often chosen it because it is described as more anabolic than androgenic, yet its documented risks include voice deepening, hirsutism, menstrual changes, clitoral enlargement and liver effects.[1]
infobox: US Schedule III; Canada Schedule IV; UK Schedule 4

paras: The reported masculinizing effects in women include voice deepening, body and facial hair growth, menstrual changes, male-pattern hair loss and clitoral enlargement, and the source notes these can persist after use stops.[1]

Searle researchers described it in 1962 and it entered US medical use in 1964. Searle discontinued Anavar in 1989 amid publicity over illicit use, and Savient launched Oxandrin in 1995. The FDA withdrew approval in 2023 citing safety and lack of proven efficacy.[1]
Bodybuilders and athletes have used it non-medically, and women are described as choosing it for its milder androgenic profile.[1]
Liver risks include peliosis hepatis and tumors, and it alters blood lipids; it is contraindicated in pregnancy and strongly potentiates warfarin.[1]
No studies found specifically on its effects on voice.

card.summary: Mild-reputation oral steroid whose documented risks in women include voice deepening that can be irreversible.
card.note: Virilization in women can be permanent; FDA approval withdrawn 2023.

quick.overview:
Oxandrolone, known as Anavar, is an oral anabolic steroid once used medically for weight recovery and used by some for physique goals, including by women.

Its article lists voice deepening and other virilizing effects in women, some of which can be irreversible.
quick.mechanism: It is an androgen receptor agonist described as strongly anabolic with weak androgenic action; virilization still occurs.
quick.risks: Documented risks include liver damage, lipid changes, virilization in women, pregnancy contraindication, drug interactions, and controlled-substance status.
